written: 2026-10-09 (Europe/Dublin), BEFORE any test was scored. Only feasibility counts (how many records contain a compass-orientation phrase) were looked at; no directions were tabulated.
purpose: Pre-registration for the PA Réalt alignment tests T1-T5 (RESEARCH.md section 6)
author: Garry Lohan (ATU Galway)

data.monuments: National Monuments Service SMR open data, SMROpenData_20251201.csv (CC BY 4.0), plus the Northern Ireland SMR nismr_10092026.geojson (OGL v3) for T4/T5 siting only; site/data/sites.json as built by scripts/build_data.py at the prereg commit
data.orientation_source: WEB_NOTES free text. The parser (scripts/orient_parse.py, to be committed BEFORE scoring and frozen) extracts only explicit 16-point compass phrases ('oriented NE-SW', 'faces E', 'axis WSW-ENE', 'opens to the SW'); a bare axis (e.g. NE-SW) is ambiguous by 180 deg, and the facing direction is used only when the text says 'faces'/'opens'/'entrance at'
data.horizon: Copernicus GLO-30 DSM horizon per site (scripts/horizon.py: 0.5 deg az step, 400 m to 60 km, k = 0.13, eye 1.6 m). Validation gate: Newgrange az 135 deg must lie within 0.1 deg of Patrick (1974) +0 deg 51 arcmin (current 0.83 deg)
data.astronomy: Declination from (az, horizon alt, latitude) with Bennett refraction; obliquity Laskar at 3200 BC (passage tombs, cursus, henges) and 2200 BC (wedge tombs, stone rows/circles/pairs, boulder-burials); lunar inclination 5.145 deg, parallax 0.95 deg

global_rules.compass_quantisation: the parsed bearings are 16-point (22.5 deg) bins; every null draw is quantised the same way (random true azimuth -> nearest 16-point bin), so the test does not reward bin artefacts
global_rules.multiple_testing: Holm-Bonferroni across the 5 primary tests at family alpha 0.05
global_rules.adoption_rule: a test 'supports an alignment' only if its Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 AND the effect has the pre-stated direction AND it survives the robustness check named for that test. Otherwise it is reported as 'not supported'. Every result is reported, whether it passes or fails
global_rules.no_peeking: no tabulation of parsed directions before scripts/orient_parse.py and this file are committed; TEST_LOG.md records commit hashes

T1.name: Wedge tombs face the setting sun (WSW-SW)
T1.population: wedge tombs with a parsed FACING direction (entrance/front)
T1.statistic: fraction of facing azimuths within the 16-point bins containing the winter-solstice sunset azimuth at that site, 2200 BC, flat horizon (primary) and DSM horizon (secondary)
T1.null: random-rotation Monte Carlo: each tomb gets a uniform random azimuth, quantised, and the same statistic is computed; plus a Rayleigh/V-test of mean direction against 236 deg
T1.robustness: holds when Cork+Kerry (the densest cluster) is excluded

T2.name: Passage tombs at solstice/equinox/standstill declinations
T2.population: passage tombs with parsed passage orientation (expected ~43) plus the surveyed featured axes; the NMS 2024 result (136 tombs, global p = 0.896) is the benchmark
T2.statistic: kernel density (sigma 1.5 deg) of declination at the 7 target declinations: +/-eps, 0, +/-(eps+i), +/-(eps-i); a summed-density score
T2.null: uniform random azimuth (quantised) through the same DSM horizon
T2.robustness: holds when Brú na Bóinne sites are excluded

T3.name: Stone rows and the lunar standstills (Ruggles replication)
T3.population: stone rows with a parsed axis (expected ~136); both ends of the axis considered and the lower-horizon end used as the 'target' end
T3.statistic: count of declinations within 1.5 deg of +/-(eps+i) and +/-(eps-i) at 2200 BC
T3.null: random azimuth Monte Carlo through each site's DSM horizon; hill-target confound: second null drawing azimuths only from local horizon maxima
T3.robustness: Cork/Kerry and the rest of Ireland analysed separately; the effect must have the same sign in both

T4.name: Passage-tomb intervisibility
T4.statistic: fraction of tombs with at least one other passage tomb within 10 km and visible (DSM line of sight), and the fraction of those where the visible tomb is higher
T4.null: the same number of points placed at random on cells with the same elevation/slope distribution within 20 km of each real cemetery (1,000 draws; this test only)
T4.robustness: Prendergast 2016 (52 of 132 directed at other tombs, 49 higher) is the published comparison, not a scored result

T5.name: Stone pairs/rows aimed at horizon peaks
T5.population: standing-stone pairs and stone rows with a parsed axis
T5.statistic: fraction of axes (either end) whose bearing bin contains a local horizon maximum of prominence >= 0.5 deg
T5.null: random azimuth Monte Carlo on each site's own horizon
T5.robustness: holds with prominence threshold 0.3 and 1.0 deg

not_tested: individual famous sites (single cases cannot be tested statistically; reported descriptively)
Martin Brennan's stellar/stone-art claims (no testable protocol)
